Guidance for Claude Code (claude.ai/code): MVP demo budget tracker. Prefer simple, readable, composable code; clear names over generic Repository, Service, Manager, etc. Avoid using comments to overexplain everything. No code comments - use descriptive method/class names instead.

Stack: .NET 10 ASP.NET Core minimal API, EF Core, nullable reference types; React 18, TypeScript strict, Vite, Tailwind, React Router v7, Axios; Docker Compose. API `src/BudgetTracker.Api/`: feature-based `Auth/`, `AntiForgery/`, endpoints in `Program.cs`. Web: auth, anti-forgery, tenant/user isolation, CSV import, AI categorization/recommendations, semantic vector search. Identity cookies + static API keys (`StaticApiKeysConfiguration`); conditional anti-forgery filtering; enforce user isolation at database query level. Azure OpenAI, pgvector, background AI recommendations, natural-language query assistance.

Commands:
`dotnet watch run`
`dotnet run -p tests/BudgetTracker.Api.Tests --output detailed --filter-query "/path/to/test"`
`dotnet ef migrations add MigrationName`
`dotnet ef database update`
`npm run dev`
`npm run build`
`npm run lint`
`docker compose up -d`
`docker compose down`

Uses Microsoft Testing Platform (not VSTest). Test names: `Should_do_when_something` (snake_case). Integration tests use Testcontainers for isolated database testing; prefer NSubstitute for mocking.

PostgreSQL: `Host=localhost;Port=5432;Database=budgettracker;Username=budgetuser;Password=budgetpass123`. API: http://localhost:5295; frontend: http://localhost:5173; Swagger: http://localhost:5295/swagger. CORS allows local ports 5295 and 5173. When one of the applications is started for testing, make sure it's stopped once finished.
